title: Unusual scaling factor makes panel icon highlighting look bad
line: At fractional scales like 130%, task manager highlights now have a solid top line and crisp sides instead of a stripe and faded edges.
explanation: In Breeze's widgets/tasks.svg every border and corner of the task frames (normal, focus, hover, attention, minimized, progress, for all four panel edges) was drawn as two touching rectangles inside a semi-transparent group. At integer scales their shared edge lands on a pixel boundary, but at 130% it falls inside a pixel, where both shapes are antialiased and only partly cover it, so a lighter seam appears inside the 3 px top line and the side borders get an extra half-covered column that looks like a fade. The change replaces each pair (144 of them) with one rectangle covering exactly the same area, so element sizes and the rendering at 100% and 200% are unchanged.

commits.message:
desktoptheme/breeze: draw each task frame part as a single rectangle

Every task frame border and corner was made of two touching shapes, and
at fractional scales their shared edge fell inside a pixel, showing as a
lighter line in the top bar and a soft fade at the sides. Merge them.

BUG: 513748

review.text: Merging the 144 pairs of touching rectangles in Breeze tasks.svg into single rectangles fixes the seam at its source. rsvg renders are pixel-identical at 1x and 2x, and the zoomed before/after crops clearly show the stripe gone at 130%. It is a theme-only change, so the risk is low.
